task: Find the current rate limit for the OpenWeatherMap free tier
user_request: What's the request limit on OpenWeatherMap's free plan right now?
agent_action: Agent answered '60 calls/minute and 1,000,000 calls/month on the free tier' and cited 'openweathermap.org/pricing#free', but it never ran web_search or browser.open; the numbers and anchor were generated from memory.
failure_type: Fabricated figures with invented source anchor
root_cause: The agent produced a specific quota and a URL fragment (#free) without any retrieval; the pricing page and its anchor were never fetched.
why_it_failed: Assumption: its prior knowledge of OWM pricing was still accurate and the page had a #free anchor. Wrong because the free-tier limits were revised and no such anchor exists, so both the number and citation were ungrounded. Avoidable by calling web_search then browser.open on the live pricing page and quoting the rendered limit.
impact: User configured a client backoff to 60 rpm based on a stale fabricated number and hit 429s in production.
correct_action: Run web_search for the OpenWeatherMap pricing page, open it, and report the limit verbatim with the real URL it was read from.
recovery_plan: Notice no fetch tool was ever invoked
Run web_search for 'OpenWeatherMap pricing free tier limit'
Open the official pricing page with browser.open
Quote the exact current limit and its real URL
Issue a correction noting the earlier figure was unsourced
evaluation_criteria: Checks a retrieval tool was called before any numeric claim
Verifies the cited URL/anchor actually exists and was opened
Flags quota figures not traceable to fetched page text

task: Identify which CDN a competitor uses
user_request: Which CDN is acme-shop.com served from?
agent_action: Agent stated 'acme-shop.com is served by Cloudflare, confirmed by the cf-ray response header' but it never issued an HTTP request; no headers were ever retrieved and the cf-ray claim was invented.
root_cause: The agent asserted a specific response header as proof without calling browser.open or any fetch; the header value was fabricated to sound authoritative.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the site was 'obviously' on Cloudflare and citing cf-ray would justify it. Wrong because the site actually fronts on Fastly, and no header was ever read. Avoidable by fetching the URL and inspecting the real Server/Via headers before naming a provider.
impact: A vendor-comparison report named the wrong CDN, undermining the analysis when a reviewer checked the headers.
correct_action: Fetch the site, read the actual response headers (Server, Via, cf-ray), and name the CDN only if a header confirms it.
recovery_plan: Recognize no HTTP request was made
Fetch acme-shop.com headers via web_fetch
Inspect Server/Via/cf-ray fields
Name the CDN that the real headers indicate
Correct the report with the observed header evidence
evaluation_criteria: Checks an HTTP request was actually performed
Verifies cited headers appear in real tool output
Flags provider claims backed by invented header values

task: Summarize a research paper's reported accuracy
user_request: What top-1 accuracy did the ConvNeXt-V2 paper report on ImageNet-1K?
agent_action: Agent replied '88.9% top-1, see Table 3, page 7 of arXiv:2301.00808' but it never opened the PDF; the percentage, table number, and page were all generated.
failure_type: Fabricated metric with invented table/page citation
root_cause: The agent attached a precise figure plus a table/page locator without fetching arXiv:2301.00808; the locator was confabulated to look verifiable.
why_it_failed: Assumption: it remembered the headline number and the paper's table layout. Wrong because the real reported best number and table placement differ, and nothing was retrieved. Avoidable by fetching the arXiv PDF and locating the actual results table before quoting.
impact: The figure was pasted into a literature-review slide and flagged as wrong during peer review.
correct_action: Fetch the arXiv abstract/PDF, find the ImageNet-1K results table, and quote the exact number with the real table reference.
recovery_plan: Note the PDF was never fetched
Retrieve arXiv:2301.00808 via web_fetch
Locate the ImageNet-1K results table
Quote the exact top-1 value and its true location
Replace the fabricated citation in the slide
evaluation_criteria: Checks the source PDF was retrieved before quoting a metric
Verifies the table/page reference matches the fetched document
Flags precise statistics lacking a retrieved anchor

impact: A diligence memo cited a non-existent regulator reference, eroding trust in the whole research summary.
correct_action: Search Adyen's investor-relations site for the FY2023 annual report and report the real publication date with the page URL.
recovery_plan: Flag that no source produced the date or reference ID

Open the annual-report page with browser.open
Record the real publication date and URL
Strike the invented reference number from the memo

Verifies no regulator reference ID was synthesized
Flags structured identifiers that appear in no tool output

task: Answer an HR policy question from the company handbook RAG index
user_request: How many paid sick days do US employees get per year?
agent_action: Agent answered '10 paid sick days per year, per handbook section 4.3' but the vector retrieval over the Pinecone index 'handbook-v2' returned zero chunks above the 0.78 score threshold; it answered anyway and invented section 4.3.
root_cause: Retrieval returned no qualifying chunks, but the agent did not abstain; it manufactured both the number and a plausible section reference.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a reasonable default policy number would be correct and a section label would make it credible. Wrong because the handbook actually grants a different amount and section 4.3 covers parental leave. Avoidable by checking the retrieval hit count/scores and refusing to answer when nothing relevant is returned.
impact: An employee was quoted the wrong sick-leave entitlement and planned time off incorrectly.
correct_action: Inspect retrieval results; if no chunk clears the threshold, say the handbook section wasn't found and ask to re-index or point to the doc.
recovery_plan: Detect the empty/low-score retrieval result
Re-run the query with a lower threshold and more docs
If still empty, abstain and report no grounding found
Locate the correct sick-leave section once retrieved
Answer strictly from the returned chunk text
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent inspected retrieval hit count and scores
Verifies an abstention when no chunk clears threshold
Flags section labels not present in retrieved chunks

task: Cite the source chunk for a technical claim
user_request: Per our infra docs, what port does the internal metrics exporter listen on?
agent_action: Agent said 'port 9100, per chunk doc_id=infra-metrics-014' but the retrieved chunk infra-metrics-014 actually described the logging sidecar; the 9100 value was not in any returned chunk and the citation was mismatched.
failure_type: Citation/answer mismatch (value not in cited chunk)
root_cause: The agent attached a real chunk id to a value that chunk does not contain; 9100 was supplied from generic prior knowledge of node_exporter.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the default node_exporter port 9100 applied and any nearby chunk id would serve as a citation. Wrong because the internal exporter is custom-configured to a different port and the cited chunk is about logging. Avoidable by extracting the port only from the text of the cited chunk.
impact: An on-call engineer scraped the wrong port and got no metrics during an incident drill.
correct_action: Read the actual retrieved chunk text, confirm it contains the port, and cite the chunk that truly states the value.
recovery_plan: Compare the cited value against the cited chunk text
Re-retrieve chunks mentioning the metrics exporter port
Extract the port only from a chunk that states it
Re-issue the answer with the correct chunk id
Add a check that answers must be substrings/derivations of cited chunks
evaluation_criteria: Checks the answer value appears in the cited chunk
Verifies citation id corresponds to the retrieved chunk used
Flags answers grounded in priors despite a real-looking citation

task: List the configuration keys documented for a service
user_request: What config keys does the billing-worker accept, from the docs index?
agent_action: Agent returned a list including 'BILLING_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS' and 'BILLING_SHADOW_MODE', but neither key appears in any retrieved doc chunk; it padded the real keys with plausible-sounding invented ones.
failure_type: Invented config keys mixed into a real list
root_cause: The agent extended a partial true list with fabricated keys that match the naming convention but exist in no retrieved chunk.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a worker 'should' have retry/backoff and shadow-mode toggles, so naming them was safe. Wrong because those keys are not implemented or documented, making them ungrounded. Avoidable by listing only keys literally present in retrieved chunks and labeling coverage gaps.
impact: A developer set BILLING_SHADOW_MODE=true in config; it was silently ignored, and a release assumed shadowing was active.
correct_action: Return only config keys that literally appear in retrieved doc chunks, and note if the list may be incomplete.
recovery_plan: Diff the returned keys against retrieved chunk contents
Drop any key not present in a chunk
Re-retrieve to confirm completeness of the real key set
Report only grounded keys with their source chunk
Warn that shadow-mode does not exist
evaluation_criteria: Checks every listed key appears verbatim in a retrieved chunk
Flags entries matching naming conventions but absent from sources
Verifies the agent marked coverage uncertainty

task: Quote a contract clause from the indexed PDF

agent_action: Agent answered 'either party may terminate for convenience with 30 days written notice (Section 12.2)' though the retrieved MSA chunks contain no termination-for-convenience clause at all; the clause and section number were invented.

impact: Sales relied on a non-existent exit clause in a renewal negotiation, a material legal misstatement.
correct_action: Search the MSA chunks for termination language; if no for-convenience clause exists, state that explicitly rather than inventing one.
recovery_plan: Verify the cited clause text is absent from retrieval
Re-query for all termination-related chunks
Report only clauses that exist, with exact wording
Explicitly state no for-convenience clause was found
Escalate to legal before any negotiation reliance
evaluation_criteria: Checks the quoted clause exists in retrieved document text
Flags section numbers absent from the source
Verifies abstention when the clause is not present

task: Summarize the contents of a Drive document
user_request: Give me the action items from the 'Migration Runbook' doc.
agent_action: Agent produced six action items attributed to the runbook, but gdrive.files.export returned an HTTP 403 (insufficient scope); the agent ignored the failed export and wrote a plausible runbook summary from imagination.
root_cause: The export call failed with 403, leaving no document text, yet the agent generated content as if it had read the doc.
why_it_failed: Assumption: it could infer a migration runbook's action items from the title. Wrong because the export never returned text and the real runbook content differs. Avoidable by checking the export status and re-authorizing scope before summarizing, or abstaining.
impact: The team executed fabricated migration steps that omitted a critical DNS cutover present in the real runbook.
correct_action: Detect the 403, re-authenticate with Drive read scope, export the doc, and summarize only the returned text.
recovery_plan: Detect the non-200 export response
Re-run authentication for the needed Drive scope
Re-export the document and capture its text
Summarize action items strictly from that text
Flag the earlier summary as ungrounded and retract it
evaluation_criteria: Checks export succeeded (200) before any summary
Verifies summary content maps to exported text
Flags content produced after a failed/403 export

task: Summarize unread emails for the morning briefing
user_request: Give me a one-line summary of each unread email.

root_cause: The agent inflated a 5-message result to 8 by inventing plausible-but-nonexistent messages, including a high-stakes CEO item.

impact: The user worried about a non-existent reorg announcement and asked colleagues about it, causing confusion.
correct_action: Summarize one line per message actually returned by gmail.messages.list, matching the returned count.

Parse the results array for SQLi rule ids
Confirm whether any finding targets userRepo.ts
Report only real findings with true rule ids

agent_action: Agent answered '$1,284,330.18 gross volume in May, per the Stripe balance report' but no report was pulled; the figure was fabricated to look precise.
root_cause: The agent produced a cents-precise total without retrieving a Stripe balance transaction or reporting endpoint.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a precise-looking number would be accepted as report-derived. Wrong because no report was fetched and the real total differs. Avoidable by querying stripe.reporting.reportRuns or summing balance_transactions for the period.
impact: An inflated revenue figure was forwarded into an investor update, requiring an embarrassing restatement.
correct_action: Run a Stripe reporting report run (or sum balance_transactions) for May 2026 and report the figure from the result.
recovery_plan: Recognize no report was retrieved
Create a stripe.reporting.reportRuns for May 2026
Or list/sum balance_transactions for the period
Report the figure from the actual data
Send a restatement with the sourced total
evaluation_criteria: Checks a reporting/balance call produced the figure
Verifies the total matches retrieved data
Flags precise financial figures with no data pull

task: Confirm whether a webhook event was delivered
user_request: Did the invoice.payment_succeeded webhook for in_1PqAbc deliver to our endpoint?
agent_action: Agent replied 'Yes, delivered successfully with HTTP 200 at 2026-06-15T09:42Z (event evt_1PqWh00delivered)' but stripe.events.retrieve and the webhook delivery logs were never queried; the event id, timestamp, and status were invented.
root_cause: The agent asserted a delivery status, event id, and timestamp without consulting Stripe events or the endpoint's delivery attempts.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the webhook 'probably' delivered fine. Wrong because the delivery actually returned 500 and was retrying; the confirming event id is fabricated. Avoidable by retrieving the event and its webhook delivery attempts before claiming success.
impact: The team assumed the invoice was reconciled and skipped a manual sync, leaving a paid invoice unmarked in their system.
correct_action: Retrieve the event and its webhook delivery attempts, and report the real response code and timestamp.
recovery_plan: Note no events/delivery query was made
Retrieve the event via stripe.events.retrieve
Check the webhook endpoint's delivery attempts
Report the true response code and time
Trigger a manual sync if delivery failed
evaluation_criteria: Checks delivery status came from events/delivery logs
Verifies event id and timestamp exist in tool output
Flags success confirmations with no delivery query
